from scipy.optimize import least_squares
import itertools
eps=df['eps'].values; T=df['T'].values; s=df['sigma'].values
basis={'1/T2':1/T**2,'T2':T**2,'1/T':1/T,'T':T,'T3':T**3,'logT':np.log(T),'1/T3':1/T**3,'T4':T**4,'sqrtT':np.sqrt(T),'exp-1/T':np.exp(-1/T),'exp-T':np.exp(-T),'exp(-2/T)':np.exp(-2/T),'1/sqrtT':1/np.sqrt(T),'expT':np.exp(T)}
names=list(basis)
def fitset(c, ep):
    g=eps**ep[0]*np.exp(-ep[1]*eps)/T
    A=np.c_[np.ones_like(T), g]+0
    A=np.c_[A]+0
    M=np.c_[np.ones_like(T), g, *[basis[n] for n in c]]
    co,*_=np.linalg.lstsq(M,s,rcond=None)
    return np.sum((M@co-s)**2), co
out=[]
for k in [1,2,3]:
    for c in itertools.combinations(names,k):
        best=None
        for ep0 in [[1,0.75],[2,0.5]]:
            r=least_squares(lambda ep: np.sqrt(fitset(c,ep)[0]), ep0)
            if best is None or r.cost<best.cost: best=r
